minutes.headline: Finance Committee reappointed a member to a three-year Capital Planning term and began planning FY21 budget talks.
minutes.summary: The town manager reported that the state committed to level FY20 unrestricted aid and Chapter 70 for FY21, plus capital plan updates and a regional CDBG award. The committee approved prior minutes, re-voted a three-year Capital Planning appointment, and debated space at TC Passios for community groups. A member reported on the school hybrid reopening plan, grants, school choice risk and the debt planning work, and the next agenda will start budget discussions.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted 7-0 by roll call to appoint its representative to a three-year term on the Capital Planning Committee.
The town manager reported the state committed to no less than the FY20 level of unrestricted aid and Chapter 70 as the FY21 baseline.
A member listed items not fully funded in FY21 (a school increase, a firefighter, a police officer, pavement management) that could be restored.
The school report covered a one-year flat teacher contract, two CARES Act grants for reopening costs, and school choice cost risk.
June 11 minutes were set for redistribution and July 23 minutes were tabled; budget discussions are set to begin at the next meeting.

why_it_matters: The state aid baseline sets the starting point for the FY21 town budget, and the underfunded lines are the ones that could be restored or left out, which affects staffing, road repair and school funding.
Reopening costs, school choice and virtual school costs can move the school budget, which is paid mostly from taxes.
watch_next: August 27 meeting: start of budget discussions, reviewing the town meeting budget with flags on deferred lines.
The June 11 minutes, redistributed for approval at the next meeting; July 23 minutes remain tabled.
